chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you fear a matter, say: 'O Allah! You are such that no one suffices from You, and You suffice from every one of Your creatures; therefore, suffice me with such and such.'

And in another hadith, he said: 'You should say: 'O Sufficer from every thing, and nothing suffices from You in the heavens and the earth! Suffice me for what worries me from the affairs of the world and the Hereafter, and send blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny.'

And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who enters upon a ruler whom he fears, let him say: 'By Allah I commence, and by Allah I shall succeed, and by Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) I divert to Him. O Allah! Ease for me his difficulty and make his harshness easy for me, for You erase what You will and confirm, and with You is the Mother of the Book.'

And you should also say: 'Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god except Him, upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Magnificent Throne. And I seek refuge by the might and strength of Allah from their might and their strength, and I seek refuge by the Lord of Al-Falaq from the evil of what He created, and there is no might nor strength except with Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications for fear and entering the presence of a ruler in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines specific supplications for navigating fear and anxiety, particularly when entering the presence of a ruler, emphasizing the concept of Allah's sufficiency (kafa'ah) as a source of spiritual strength. It integrates Quranic verses such as Ayat al-Kursi and Surah Al-Falaq to provide a comprehensive framework for seeking protection from both external threats and internal worries, reflecting the Shia tradition of combining verbal invocation with divine attributes. The text highlights the practical application of tawakkul (trust in God) in high-stakes social and political interactions, reinforcing the belief that Allah alone is the ultimate protector and decider of affairs.
